title: Structures that must resist bending are built as hollow tubes

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Structures that must resist bending are built as hollow tubes

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Where stiffness against bending in all directions is required, organisms use a hollow cylindrical construction with little or no material in the core, as in the thin-walled, almost empty wing bones of long-winged birds such as the albatross, quills, and hollow stems of reeds and straw.

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. XVI: On Form and Mechanical Efficiency

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: it is appropriate in every case where _stiffness_ is required, where bending has to be resisted. The long bone of a bird’s wing has little or no weight to carry, but it has to withstand powerful bending moments; and in the arm-bone of a long-winged bird, such as an albatross, we see the tubular construction manifested in its perfection

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci On Growth and Form claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: D’Arcy Wentworth Thompson, On Growth and Form (1st ed., Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1917), Chapter XVI, “On Form and Mechanical Efficiency”; topic “Tubular construction of bones and stems”. Scope: long bones of vertebrates (especially bird wing bones), feather quills and cylindrical plant stems

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on thompson1917-ch16-03: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.68

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Hollowness and bending efficiency are measurable, but “where required” risks selecting cases by the outcome. Open scans support broad comparative tests, though functional loading and full taxonomic coverage remain incomplete.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Quantify cross-sectional hollowness and second moment of area in structures exposed to multidirectional bending, comparing them with structures under other dominant loads while controlling size. Frequent solid cores in the target class would refute the generalization.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The scope combines nonhomologous animal and plant structures.

Loading regime is not encoded with most scans.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Cross-sectional geometry of long bones is measurable on open CT and on at least one tabulated femur series. Linking hollowness specifically to omnidirectional bending requires an independent load classification, and many hollow organs have other functions. The comparison can be run for bird wing bones versus some limb bones and remains a proxy for the full design claim, including plants and quills.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Measure the hollowness index (inner versus outer radius, or second-moment contribution of the cortex) in structures that carry bending in all directions and in structures loaded mainly in compression. Support would be thin-walled tubes in bird wing bones, quills and reed stems, and solid or thick-walled sections where bending is small; hollow compression members and solid bending members would refute the design rule.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Hollowness also serves marrow, pneumatization and mass reduction, so bending stiffness is not isolated by the cross-section alone.

Quills and reed stems are thinly represented beside vertebrate bone scans.
